answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identity creation to an operating system kernel enforcing memory-hard challenges. During verification, pseudorandom pointers wander through a dense willow graph in RAM, forcing an adversary to expend dedicated memory bandwidth and energy per identity. Although this imposes a verifiable hardware cost, the mechanism remains limited by hardware asymmetry, as adversaries with custom memory architectures can generate proofs at lower marginal costs.
